mainTopic: The wording of the זימון, who may split up or join for a זימון, and the new משנה on dividing groups
overview: This amud is all about the זימון, the group invitation to say ברכת המזון together. It opens by ruling that the leader may say 'בָּרְכוּ', but 'נְבָרֵךְ' (which includes himself) is better. The proof is that a group of six may split into two groups of three. A ברייתא then teaches that a person's ברכות show whether he is a תלמיד חכם, and several wording rules follow: 'וּבְטוּבוֹ', 'חָיִינוּ', no 'לְמִי', and not 'עַל הַמָּזוֹן' in a זימון of three. The גמרא then explains a contradiction in the משנה about whether the wording grows with a bigger crowd: it is a מחלוקת between רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא, and רבא rules like רבי עקיבא. Stories follow about meals at the ריש גלותא's house, a rule that there is no זימון למפרע, and רפרם's mistake about 'ברכו את ה׳ המבורך'. A new משנה teaches when a group may split up, when two groups combine, and the מחלוקת about blessing on undiluted wine. The גמרא asks why the משנה repeats that three may not split, and it gives several answers, ending with רב חסדא's limit. רבא's comment that follows continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Both wordings are allowed, but 'Let us bless' is better
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the leader may even say בָּרְכוּ, but נְבָרֵךְ is preferable.
steps.simpleTranslation: He may even say 'Bless!', but in any case 'Let us bless' is preferable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier discussion about how to word the זימון. It rules that saying בָּרְכוּ is acceptable, but נְבָרֵךְ is the better choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא had a tension between שמואל, who said a person should never exclude himself from the group, and a source that allowed בָּרְכוּ. The resolution is that both are valid, so the source allowing בָּרְכוּ is not wrong. שמואל's point is only about which wording is preferable: נְבָרֵךְ includes the leader in the group.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Bless!' — the leader tells the others to bless, which leaves himself out
'Let us bless' — the leader includes himself in the group

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think בָּרְכוּ is wrong or invalid. The ruling is that both are allowed, and only one of them is preferable.

phrases.english: Even 'Bless!' (may be said),
phrases.notes: This continues a discussion that began on the previous amud.

phrases.english: but in any case 'Let us bless' is preferable,

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף בָּרְכוּ וּמִכׇּל מָקוֹם נְבָרֵךְ עֲדִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the earlier tension (from the previous daf) between שמואל and a source that permits בָּרְכוּ.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both options are valid; the dispute is only about which is preferable
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think that saying בָּרְכוּ goes against שמואל and is wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: בָּרְכוּ is permitted, but נְבָרֵךְ is preferable.

steps.title: Source: groups of six to ten may split up
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה quotes a teaching from the school of רב: groups of six up to ten people may divide into separate זימון groups.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב אדא בר אהבה said that they said in the school of רב: We learned: six people may divide, up to ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to prove that נְבָרֵךְ is preferable. This step only presents the source; the next step explains how it proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that a group of six (up to ten) may split into two groups, as long as each smaller group still has at least three people for a זימון. Ten does not split, because together they can mention שם ה' in the זימון. This rule is the raw material for the proof in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They said in the school (בית מדרש) of רב

phrases.english: As Rav Adda bar Ahava said,
they said in the school of Rav: We learned:
Six may divide, up to ten.
phrases.notes: A group of six to ten may split into two groups, each doing its own זימון.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמְרִי בֵּי רַב תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support the ruling that נְבָרֵךְ is preferable.
steps.raayaObject: That נְבָרֵךְ is the preferred wording
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of בי רב: שִׁשָּׁה נֶחְלָקִין עַד עֲשָׂרָה

steps.title: Why splitting proves 'Let us bless' is better
steps.stepSummary: Splitting only makes sense if נְבָרֵךְ is preferable. If בָּרְכוּ were better, splitting would cost each group the better wording, so the rule proves נְבָרֵךְ is preferable.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say 'Let us bless' is preferable — that is why they may divide. But if you say 'Bless!' is preferable — why may they divide? Rather, must we not learn from this that 'Let us bless' is preferable? Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the rule about splitting proves its point. It then confirms the conclusion with 'שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With בָּרְכוּ, the leader speaks to others and leaves himself out. So he would need at least three others in front of him, and a group of three would not be enough for the 'better' form. If בָּרְכוּ were preferable, splitting six into two groups of three would push both groups into the weaker wording, and we would not allow it. Since we do allow splitting, the leader must be counted as part of the group, and that is exactly what נְבָרֵךְ expresses.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say…
Learn from it (the proof is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: The זימון is best said as נְבָרֵךְ, which includes the leader. This is proven from the rule that six to ten may split into separate groups.

phrases.english: It works well if you say 'Let us bless' is preferable —
that is why they may divide,
but if you say 'Bless!' is preferable —
why may they divide?!
phrases.notes: Splitting would cause each group to lose the preferred wording.

phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from this that 'Let us bless' is preferable?
Learn from it (indeed).

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא נְבָרֵךְ עֲדִיף מִשּׁוּם הָכִי נֶחְלָקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the source in step 2 proves the ruling in step 1.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The permission for six to ten to split into separate זימון groups
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: נְבָרֵךְ is the preferred wording for the זימון.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports this: no criticism, except from the careful
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that we do not criticize someone for saying either בָּרְכוּ or נְבָרֵךְ, but careful, precise people do criticize him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught so: Whether he said 'Bless!' or he said 'Let us bless,' we do not criticize him for it, but the precise ones criticize him for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches its conclusion. Both wordings are acceptable, but there is still a more careful, preferable way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אין תופסין אותו' shows that both wordings are valid. 'הנקדנין תופסין אותו' shows there is still a better choice that careful people insist on. This fits exactly with 'אף בָּרְכוּ, ומכל מקום נְבָרֵךְ עדיף'.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא)

phrases.english: It was also taught so:
Whether he said 'Bless!' or he said 'Let us bless' —
we do not criticize him for it,
but the precise ones do criticize him for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא that supports the conclusion reached in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: Both wordings are valid, but one is more precise

steps.title: A person's blessings reveal whether he is a scholar
steps.stepSummary: A person's ברכות show whether he is a תלמיד חכם. רבי says that saying 'וּבְטוּבוֹ' marks a תלמיד חכם, while 'וּמִטּוּבוֹ' marks a בור.
steps.simpleTranslation: From a person's blessings it is recognizable whether he is a Torah scholar or not. How so? רבי says: 'And by His goodness' — he is a Torah scholar; 'And from His goodness' — he is an ignoramus.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a new idea: the small wording choices in ברכות show a person's level of learning. רבי gives an example from the זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The זימון says 'ברוך שאכלנו משלו ובטובו חיינו', meaning we live by His goodness. Saying 'מטובו' (from His goodness) suggests we got only part of His goodness, which shrinks ה''s kindness. So the one-letter difference shows whether the speaker understands what he is saying.

keyTerms.meaning: And by His goodness (the full goodness)
And from His goodness (only part of it)

steps.confusionAlert: The difference is only one letter: ב (by) versus מ (from). The ב means we live by His full goodness. The מ wrongly suggests we received only a portion of it.

phrases.english: And from a person's blessings it is recognizable

phrases.aramaic: אִם תַּלְמִיד חָכָם הוּא אִם לָאו.
phrases.english: whether he is a Torah scholar or not.
How so? Rabbi says:
'And by His goodness' — this is a Torah scholar,
'And from His goodness' — this is an ignoramus.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִבִּרְכוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם נִיכָּר אִם תַּלְמִיד חָכָם הוּא אִם לָאו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא but moves to a new wording issue in the זימון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Say 'וּבְטוּבוֹ', not 'וּמִטּוּבוֹ'; the wording shows whether one is a תלמיד חכם.

steps.title: אביי challenges from דוד המלך's 'from Your blessing'
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב דימי: דוד המלך himself said 'וּמִבִּרְכָתְךָ' (from Your blessing), so how can the 'from' wording be wrong?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב דימי: But isn't it written: 'And from Your blessing may Your servant's house be blessed forever'?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבי's rule. A פסוק shows דוד המלך using the 'from' (מ) wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If saying 'מ' (from) means a person is a בור, how could דוד המלך use 'מִבִּרְכָתְךָ' in a תפילה recorded in the תנ"ך? The פסוק seems to show that the 'from' wording is perfectly proper.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written…? (introduces a challenge from a פסוק)

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Dimi:
But isn't it written:
'And from Your blessing may Your servant's house be blessed forever'!
phrases.notes: שמואל ב ז:כט — דוד המלך's תפילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב דִּימִי וְהָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי's rule from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's statement that 'מטובו' is the wording of a בור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דוד המלך used the 'from' (מ) wording, so it cannot be improper.

steps.title: A request is different
steps.stepSummary: When asking for something, it is proper to ask humbly for only part of ה''s blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a request it is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי. דוד המלך was making a request, and that is a different situation from praising ה' in a ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a ברכה of praise, we must describe ה''s goodness as complete, so 'by His goodness' is correct. In a request, it is humble and fitting not to demand all of ה''s blessing, so 'from Your blessing' is fine there.

phrases.english: With a request it is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is improper in praise, but fitting in a humble request.

steps.title: Challenge: even in requests, ask for a lot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. The פסוק 'הַרְחֶב פִּיךָ וַאֲמַלְּאֵהוּ' suggests that even in requests one should ask for everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a request too — isn't it written: 'Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 7 with another פסוק. This פסוק seems to encourage asking ה' for a lot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a request should be humble and ask only for part, why does ה' say 'open your mouth wide and I will fill it'? That sounds like we should ask for the full amount even when making a request.

keyTerms.meaning: Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it (תהלים פא:יא)

phrases.english: With a request too — isn't it written:
'Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a request should be humble and ask only for part
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק tells us to ask for a lot, so a request does not need to be limited.

steps.title: That verse is about Torah learning
steps.stepSummary: 'הַרְחֶב פִּיךָ' refers to דברי תורה, where asking for as much as possible is proper.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is written about matters of Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The פסוק about opening your mouth wide speaks only about asking for Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For תורה, one should ask without limits. For material blessings, a humble request for part of ה''s blessing is proper. So דוד המלך's 'מִבִּרְכָתְךָ' fits, and רבי's rule for ברכות of praise stays in place.
steps.whatToRemember: In praising ה', say וּבְטוּבוֹ (His full goodness). In a request for material things, a humble 'from Your blessing' is fine. For Torah, ask for as much as possible.

phrases.english: That one is written about matters of Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8 and keeps the answer from step 7 standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the פסוק to a specific area (Torah)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every request should be for the full amount.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only for Torah should one ask without limit; other requests should be humble.

steps.title: רבי: 'We live' is correct, 'they live' is wrong
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי: in the זימון, saying 'בטובו חיינו' marks a תלמיד חכם, while saying 'חיים' marks a בור.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי says: one who says 'by His goodness we live' is a תלמיד חכם. One who says 'they live' is a בור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another example of how a person's ברכה wording shows whether he is a תלמיד חכם. This time the question is whether to say 'we live' or 'they live' in the זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line in the זימון is 'וּבְטוּבוֹ חָיִינוּ', meaning 'and by His goodness we live'. Saying 'חיים' ('they live') sounds as if the leader is leaving himself out of the group. That is why רבי calls it the wording of a בור.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi says:
'By His goodness we live' —
phrases.notes: This is part of the זימון response: 'וּבְטוּבוֹ חָיִינוּ'.

phrases.english: this person is a Torah scholar;
'they live' — this person is an ignoramus.
phrases.notes: He leaves himself out of the group.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second wording test from רבי, alongside the earlier 'ובטובו / ומטובו' test.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the זימון, 'בטובו חיינו' (we live) is correct. 'חיים' (they live) is incorrect.

steps.title: The scholars of נהרבלא reverse the version
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of נהרבלא teach the opposite: 'חיים' is the better wording and 'חיינו' is the worse one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The scholars of נהרבלא teach it the other way around.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a different version of רבי's teaching, held by the scholars of נהרבלא. This sets up the ruling that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the נהרבלא version, 'חיים' ('they live') is preferred because it sounds broader: it includes all living beings and is not just about ourselves. So the same two wordings are judged in exactly the opposite way.

keyTerms.meaning: The scholars of the town of נהרבלא
They teach (they have this version of the text)

phrases.english: The scholars of Neharbela teach the opposite;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a reversed version of the ברייתא in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the נהרבלא version, 'חיים' is preferred over 'חיינו'.

steps.title: The הלכה does not follow נהרבלא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה does not follow the נהרבלא version. One should say 'חיינו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is not like the scholars of נהרבלא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles which version we follow: the standard version of רבי, not the reversed one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the הלכה rejects the נהרבלא version, the practical wording stays 'ובטובו חיינו'. The leader includes himself with everyone else.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה is not (like this view)

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is why the זימון we say today has 'וּבְטוּבוֹ חָיִינוּ'.

phrases.english: And the halakha is not like the scholars of Neharbela.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between step 10 and step 11 in favor of step 10.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: say 'Let us bless the One whose food we ate', not 'to whom'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that 'נברך שאכלנו משלו' marks a תלמיד חכם, while 'למי שאכלנו משלו' marks a בור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: one who says 'Let us bless the One whose food we ate' is a תלמיד חכם. One who says 'Let us bless to the one whose food we ate' is a בור.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives another wording test, this time for the opening invitation of the זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding 'למי' ('to the one who') makes the sentence sound as if we are blessing a person, namely the host who served the food. Without 'למי', the sentence clearly refers to הקב"ה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
'Let us bless the One whose food we have eaten'
— this person is a Torah scholar;
'to the one whose food we have eaten'
— this person is an ignoramus.
phrases.notes: It sounds like blessing the host.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: נְבָרֵךְ שֶׁאָכַלְנוּ מִשֶּׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new wording rule about the זימון, now from the אמורא רבי יוחנן rather than the תנא רבי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not add 'למי' to the זימון invitation.

steps.title: Challenge: we do say 'to the One who' at the סדר
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי: the הגדה says 'למי שעשה לאבותינו ולנו את כל הנסים האלו', so why is 'למי' wrong?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא the son of רבא said to רב אשי: But we say 'to the One who did all these miracles for our fathers and for us'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's rule by pointing to a well-known text that uses the exact wording he rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'למי' were a problem, it should be a problem in the הגדה too. Yet there it is the accepted wording.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha the son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:
But don't we say:
'To the One who did for our fathers and for us'
'all these miracles'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that 'למי' is the wording of a בור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The accepted הגדה text uses 'למי', which shows that 'למי' cannot be wrong in itself.

steps.title: Answer: with miracles, it is obvious who is meant
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers: in the הגדה it is obvious that 'למי' refers to הקב"ה, because only He performs miracles.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, the matter is clear. Who performs miracles? הקב"ה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains why 'למי' is fine in the הגדה but not in the זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with 'למי' is only that it can be misunderstood as referring to a person. With miracles, no one could think a human is meant. With food, the host really did provide it, so the wording is misleading.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, blessed be He

phrases.english: He said to him: There, the matter is self-evident;
who performs miracles? —
The Holy One, blessed be He.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends step 13 against the challenge in step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'למי' is always a wrong wording, so the הגדה should be wrong too.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'למי' is only a problem where it could be mistaken for a human. Miracles can only refer to הקב"ה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: say 'Blessed is the One whose food we ate', not 'for the food we ate'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that 'ברוך שאכלנו משלו' marks a תלמיד חכם, while 'על המזון שאכלנו' marks a בור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: one who says 'Blessed is the One whose food we ate' is a תלמיד חכם. One who says 'for the food we ate' is a בור.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives one more wording rule, this time for the response in the זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'על המזון' limits the praise to the food alone. That sounds like thanking the host for his meal, not praising הקב"ה, who gives everything (תוספות).
steps.whatToRemember: In the זימון, the wording must clearly point to הקב"ה and include the person speaking. Say 'חיינו' (not 'חיים'). Avoid 'למי', because it could sound like the host. In a זימון of three, say 'שאכלנו משלו', not 'על המזון' (the next step limits this rule to three).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
'Blessed is the One whose food we have eaten'
— this person is a Torah scholar;
'for the food that we have eaten'
— this person is an ignoramus.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בָּרוּךְ שֶׁאָכַלְנוּ מִשֶּׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another wording rule from רבי יוחנן, this time about the response to the זימון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Respond 'ברוך שאכלנו משלו', not 'על המזון שאכלנו'.

steps.title: The criticism only applies to a group of three
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע limits רבי יוחנן's rule. Saying 'על המזון שאכלנו' is only a problem in a זימון of three, where God's name is not mentioned. In a זימון of ten, God's name is said, so it is obvious who is being blessed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, the son of רב יהושע, said: We only said this about a group of three, where God's name is not mentioned. But with ten, where God's name is mentioned, the meaning is clear.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא limits the rule from the previous step. He says it only applies to a group of three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With three people, the leader says 'ברוך שאכלנו' without God's name. So 'על המזון שאכלנו' would sound like we are thanking the food or the host, not God. With ten, God's name is said right before, so 'על המזון שאכלנו' clearly refers to Him.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this in the case of; a phrase that limits an earlier rule
The matter is self-evident; it is clear from the context
The group invitation to say ברכת המזון together

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that wording is judged by context. The same words can be fine in one setting and misleading in another.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
We only said this with regard to three,
where there is no mention of God's name,
but with ten, where there is mention of God's name —
the matter is self-evident,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי יוחנן's ruling from step 16 to a זימון of three.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'על המזון שאכלנו' is only the mark of a בור in a זימון of three. With ten, where God's name is said, it is acceptable.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה's formula for ten
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רב הונא from the משנה. In a group of ten, the response itself ends with 'על המזון שאכלנו', right after God's name and titles.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in the משנה: Just as he blesses, so they answer after him: 'Blessed is ה' the God of Israel, the God of Hosts, Who sits upon the כרובים, for the food that we have eaten.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to show that 'על המזון שאכלנו' is fine when God's name comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה itself uses the exact phrase that רבי יוחנן criticized, but it uses it in the ten-person formula. That would be impossible unless the phrase is acceptable once God's name makes the meaning clear. So the משנה backs up רב הונא's limit.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Who sits upon the כרובים, a title of God

phrases.english: as we learned in the mishna:

phrases.aramaic: כָּעִנְיָן שֶׁהוּא מְבָרֵךְ, כָּךְ עוֹנִין אַחֲרָיו:
phrases.english: Just as he blesses, so they respond after him:
"Blessed is the Lord, God of Israel,
God of Hosts, Who sits upon the cherubs,
for the food that we have eaten."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a proof from the משנה for רב הונא's limit.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that 'על המזון שאכלנו' is acceptable when God's name is mentioned.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's formula for a זימון of ten, which ends 'על המזון שאכלנו'.
steps.whatToRemember: 'על המזון שאכלנו' is only a problem in a זימון of three. With ten, God's name makes the meaning clear, and the משנה itself uses that phrase.

steps.title: The משנה seems to contradict itself about group size
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: 'the same for ten and for one hundred thousand.' That means the size of the group does not matter. Yet the same משנה then gives different wording for one hundred, one thousand, and ten thousand.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The same for ten and for one hundred thousand.' This itself is difficult! You said ten and one hundred thousand are the same, so they are equal. And then it teaches: with a hundred he says this, with a thousand he says this, with ten thousand he says this!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and points out that it clashes with a later line in the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first line says the wording never changes once there are ten people. The later lines say the wording grows as the group gets bigger. Both cannot be true in one משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: This itself is difficult; the source contradicts itself
They are the same as each other

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack from an outside source. The contradiction is between two lines of the same משנה.

phrases.english: Both ten and ten myriads (one hundred thousand).
This itself is difficult:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרַתְּ אֶחָד עֲשָׂרָה וְאֶחָד עֲשָׂרָה רִבּוֹא,
phrases.english: you said, both ten and ten myriads,
evidently they are the same;
and then it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: בְּמֵאָה אוֹמֵר, בְּאֶלֶף אוֹמֵר, בְּרִבּוֹא אוֹמֵר!
phrases.english: with a hundred he says, with a thousand he says, with ten thousand he says!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the internal consistency of the משנה about group size.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement 'אחד עשרה ואחד עשרה רבוא'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Internal contradiction. One clause makes all groups of ten or more equal, while another clause gives a different formula for each larger group.

steps.title: Two different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the two lines of the משנה follow two different opinions. One follows רבי יוסי הגלילי and the other follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It is not difficult. This line is רבי יוסי הגלילי, and that line is רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף resolves the contradiction by assigning each line of the משנה to a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is not contradicting itself. It records an argument. The changing wording for bigger groups follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, and the 'same for ten and ten thousand' line follows רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: This one ... that one; assigning each source to a different view

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It is not difficult;

phrases.aramaic: הָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, הָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.english: this is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, that is Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, הָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the internal contradiction raised in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the source between two תנאים (תרי תנאי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is one opinion that contradicts itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה records two opposing opinions. רבי יוסי הגלילי changes the wording by group size, and רבי עקיבא does not.

steps.title: Showing the two opinions in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the משנה, where רבי יוסי הגלילי rules that the wording depends on the size of the crowd and learns it from 'במקהלות ברכו אלהים'. רבי עקיבא compares it to the synagogue, where the wording stays the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי יוסי הגלילי says, they bless according to the size of the crowd, as it says 'In assemblies bless God.' רבי עקיבא said: What do we find in the synagogue, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב יוסף's answer by showing that the משנה really does contain these two opposing views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי reads 'במקהלות' (in assemblies) as a source for adding praise as the group grows. רבי עקיבא learns from the synagogue. There, once ten are present, the leader says 'ברכו' the same way no matter how many come.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the size of the crowd
What do we find; a comparison to a known case
Etcetera; the rest of the quote is assumed

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
According to the size of the crowd they bless,
as it is stated: "In assemblies bless God."

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: מַה מָּצִינוּ בְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said: What do we find in the synagogue, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יוסף's answer by citing the two opinions from the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that the משנה contains two opposing views.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה, where רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא argue.

steps.title: How does רבי עקיבא use the פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי עקיבא does with the פסוק 'במקהלות ברכו אלהים'. He does not use it to change the wording by group size.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא, what does he do with this פסוק of רבי יוסי הגלילי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a standard question. If רבי עקיבא rejects רבי יוסי הגלילי's reading, what does he learn from that פסוק?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word of a פסוק is assumed to teach something. Since רבי עקיבא does not learn group-size wording from 'במקהלות', the גמרא wants to know what lesson he takes from it.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? How does he use this פסוק?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva,

phrases.aramaic: הַאי קְרָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: this verse of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי קְרָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the dispute by asking how רבי עקיבא uses רבי יוסי הגלילי's פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי עקיבא learns from 'במקהלות ברכו אלהים'.

steps.title: Even unborn babies sang at the sea
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא needs the פסוק for רבי מאיר's teaching. Even babies still in their mothers' wombs sang שירה at the ים סוף, as it says 'במקהלות ברכו אלהים ה׳ ממקור ישראל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what was taught: רבי מאיר used to say, from where do we know that even babies in their mothers' wombs sang the song at the sea? As it says: 'In assemblies bless God, ה׳, from the source of Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא uses the פסוק for a different lesson, taught by רבי מאיר in a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי עקיבא, 'במקהלות' refers to the whole nation at the sea, including unborn babies. 'ממקור ישראל' (from the source of Israel) hints at the womb. So the פסוק is used up on this lesson and does not teach anything about the זימון.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it for another teaching
For that which was taught in a ברייתא
Unborn babies in their mothers' wombs
The song at the ים סוף (אז ישיר)

phrases.english: He needs it for that which was taught:
Rabbi Meir would say:
From where do we know that even fetuses in their mothers' wombs
sang the song at the sea?
As it is stated: "In assemblies bless God,
the Lord, from the source of Israel."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22 by giving רבי עקיבא's use of the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא uses the פסוק for רבי מאיר's teaching that even unborn babies sang at the sea.

steps.title: Where does רבי יוסי הגלילי learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the other side. רבי יוסי הגלילי uses 'במקהלות' for the זימון, so how does he know that unborn babies sang at the sea?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one?
steps.whatsHappening: In one word, the גמרא turns to רבי יוסי הגלילי and asks where he learns the lesson about the unborn babies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי already used 'במקהלות' for changing the wording by group size. So the גמרא asks whether he disagrees about the babies, or whether he learns it from somewhere else.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one? How does the other opinion handle this?

phrases.english: And the other one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the mirror question for רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי יוסי הגלילי knows that unborn babies sang at the sea.

steps.title: He learns it from the word 'ממקור'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns the lesson about the unborn babies from the word 'ממקור' (from the source), which hints at the womb. That leaves 'במקהלות' free for the זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: He derives it from 'ממקור'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי הגלילי gets the babies' song from a different word in the same פסוק. This closes the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each part of the פסוק teaches something different. For רבי יוסי הגלילי, 'ממקור' teaches about the babies and 'במקהלות' teaches about the זימון. For רבי עקיבא, the whole פסוק is needed for the babies.

keyTerms.meaning: It is derived; it comes out from
Source; here a hint to the mother's womb

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's two lines are two opinions. רבי יוסי הגלילי adds praise to the זימון for bigger groups, learning from 'במקהלות'. רבי עקיבא keeps the same wording for any group of ten or more, comparing it to the synagogue. Each one uses the פסוק in his own way.

phrases.english: He derives it from "from the source."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24 and closes the discussion of how each תנא reads the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns about the unborn babies from 'ממקור', leaving 'במקהלות' for the זימון.

steps.title: רבא rules like רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא, so the זימון wording does not change with the size of the group.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling in the argument between רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא. The הלכה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי said the wording grows with the crowd (100, 1,000, 10,000). רבי עקיבא compared it to shul, where the wording stays the same. רבא decides for רבי עקיבא: once there are ten, the wording is fixed no matter how many more people join.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows this opinion
A leading אמורא of Bavel who often gives final rulings

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, the זימון wording for ten is the same as for a hundred or more. This is רבי עקיבא's view.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Akiva.
phrases.notes: The wording does not change once there are ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the argument whose sources were just explained in steps 21-25.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Once there are ten people, the זימון wording is the same no matter how big the group is.

steps.title: רבינא stops רב חמא from gathering one hundred people
steps.stepSummary: At the ריש גלותא's house, רב חמא tried to gather 100 people for a bigger זימון. רבינא told him it is unnecessary because the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא and רב חמא בר בוזי came to the house of the ריש גלותא. רב חמא got up and started looking around to gather one hundred people. רבינא said to him: You don't need to, because רבא said the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: This story shows רבא's ruling being used in real life. רבינא uses it to stop an effort that is not needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חמא was acting like רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds that 100 people get a special wording. רבינא reminds him that the ruling follows רבי עקיבא, so gathering 100 changes nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, the political leader of the Jews in Bavel
They happened to come to a place
Searching for, going around to gather

phrases.english: Ravina and Rav Hama bar Buzi
happened to come to the house of the Exilarch.
Rav Hama rose
and was going around to gather a group of one hundred.
phrases.notes: He wanted the special wording for 100 people.

phrases.english: Ravina said to him: You don't need to,
for this is what Rava said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא וְרַב חָמָא בַּר בּוּזִי אִקְּלַעוּ לְבֵי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבא's ruling from step 26 in a real case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no need to gather 100 people for a special זימון, because the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: At the ריש גלותא's house they bentched in groups of three
steps.stepSummary: רבא reports that at the ריש גלותא's meals, the חכמים made זימון in small groups of three.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: When we ate bread at the house of the ריש גלותא, we would bentch in groups of three.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא describes a practice. This sets up the next two questions about why they did it this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were many people at the meal, so they could have made a זימון of ten. Instead they split into groups of three. The גמרא will now ask why.

keyTerms.meaning: We would say the ברכה, here ברכת המזון

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אָכְלִינַן רִפְתָּא בֵּי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא,
phrases.english: When we would eat bread at the house of the Exilarch,
we would bless in groups of three.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כִּי אָכְלִינַן רִפְתָּא בֵּי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: how the חכמים handled זימון at the ריש גלותא's meals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At the ריש גלותא's house, רבא and his colleagues bentched with a זימון of three.

steps.title: Why not bentch in groups of ten?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the practice: they should have made a larger זימון of ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them bentch in groups of ten!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to רבא's practice. With so many people there, they should have made a זימון of ten, which includes ה׳'s name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זימון of ten is a higher level, because it adds 'אלהינו'. Choosing three when ten was available looks like giving up something better for no reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Let them say the ברכה (said as a challenge)

phrases.english: Let them bless in groups of ten!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practice described in step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of bentching in groups of three
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A זימון of ten with ה׳'s name was possible and is better, so why settle for three?

steps.title: The ריש גלותא would be offended
steps.stepSummary: A זימון of ten would be loud and noticeable, and the ריש גלותא would hear and be upset.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ריש גלותא would hear and get angry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. A big group of ten would draw attention, and the ריש גלותא would be upset.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ריש גלותא was still eating. Seeing a large group of חכמים bentch before he finished would look disrespectful. Small groups of three were quieter and less noticeable.

keyTerms.meaning: And he would become angry or offended

phrases.english: The Exilarch would hear and become angry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 29.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed nothing stopped them from making a זימון of ten.
steps.terutzMaskana: Respect for the ריש גלותא made them choose quieter groups of three.

steps.title: Why not join the ריש גלותא's own bentching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why they did not simply fulfill their obligation by hearing the ריש גלותא's זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them fulfill their obligation with the ריש גלותא's bentching!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second challenge. Why not wait and be יוצא with the ריש גלותא's large זימון, which would avoid offending him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only concern was upsetting the ריש גלותא, there seems to be an easy fix: bentch together with him. Then they get a large זימון and show him respect.

keyTerms.meaning: Let them be יוצא (fulfill their obligation)
The ברכה (here, the זימון and ברכת המזון)

phrases.english: Let them fulfill their obligation with the blessing of the Exilarch!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 30 by offering another option.
steps.kashyaTarget: The decision to bentch separately instead of with the ריש גלותא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Joining the ריש גלותא's זימון would avoid offending him and still give a large זימון.

steps.title: Too much noise to hear
steps.stepSummary: At such a big, noisy meal, people could not hear the ריש גלותא's bentching, so they could not be יוצא with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since everyone was making noise, they would not hear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge. The room was too loud to hear the ריש גלותא's ברכה clearly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To be יוצא with someone else's ברכה, you must actually hear it. In a crowded, noisy hall that was not possible, so they needed their own small זימון.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a basic rule: you can only be יוצא with another person's ברכה if you actually hear it.

phrases.english: Since everyone is making noise,
they do not hear.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַיְּידֵי דְּאָוְושׁוּ כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא שָׁמְעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 31 and closes this topic.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reason that blocks the suggested option
steps.terutzHavaAmina: They could just listen to the ריש גלותא's bentching.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of the noise they could not hear, so they made their own groups of three.

steps.title: One who bentched alone first: no retroactive זימון
steps.stepSummary: Three people ate together, and one bentched by himself first. The other two can still make a זימון with him, but he gains nothing from it, because a זימון cannot work backwards.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה תוספאה said: Three people ate bread together, and one of them went ahead and bentched on his own. The other two are יוצא with זימון through him. He is not יוצא with זימון through them, because there is no זימון backwards.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה תוספאה gives a new rule. It covers a case where one of the three bentched alone before the group made a זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other two still need a זימון, and he can answer to complete their group of three. But his own ברכת המזון is already done, so a later זימון cannot go back and attach to it. The others gain the זימון; he does not.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא from a later generation

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean his ברכת המזון was invalid. He did fulfill ברכת המזון. He only loses the extra מצוה of זימון, while the other two still get it through him.

phrases.english: Rabba Tosefa'a said:

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּכָרְכִי רִפְתָּא בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי,
phrases.english: These three who break bread together,
and one of them went ahead
and bentched on his own,
they fulfill their obligation with zimmun through him,
he does not fulfill zimmun through them,
because there is no retroactive zimmun.
phrases.notes: A זימון cannot attach to a ברכה that was already said.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה תּוֹסְפָאָה: הָנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּכָרְכִי רִפְתָּא בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate rule about זימון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If one of three bentched alone, the other two can still make a זימון with him, but he does not gain זימון, because there is no זימון למפרע.

steps.title: רפרם בר פפא leaves out 'המבורך' and the shul protests
steps.stepSummary: Back to the משנה's argument about the shul wording. רפרם בר פפא said only 'ברכו את ה׳' at the Torah reading, and the whole shul called out 'ברכו את ה׳ המבורך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'רבי ישמעאל says' (from the משנה). רפרם בר פפא came to the shul of אבי גיבר. He got up to read from the Torah, said 'ברכו את ה׳', and stopped without saying 'המבורך'. Everyone called out: 'ברכו את ה׳ המבורך!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה, 'רבי ישמעאל אומר', and tells a story about it. This story sets up רבא's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי עקיבא says the shul wording is 'ברכו את ה׳', while רבי ישמעאל adds 'המבורך'. רפרם followed רבי עקיבא. The people in that shul were used to רבי ישמעאל's wording, so they protested out loud.

keyTerms.meaning: Quote of the משנה's words, marking the next topic
'The blessed One', the extra word in רבי ישמעאל's wording

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says.
Rafram bar Pappa
happened to come to the synagogue of Avi Givar,
he rose and read from the Torah scroll
and said: 'Bless the Lord,'
and was silent, and did not say: 'the blessed One.'
Everyone cried out:
'Bless the Lord, the blessed One!'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר. רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא אִקְּלַע לְבֵי כְּנִישְׁתָּא דַּאֲבִי גִיבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next part of the משנה: the argument between רבי עקיבא and רבי ישמעאל about the shul wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רפרם followed רבי עקיבא and left out 'המבורך', and the community objected.

steps.title: רבא: why get involved in the dispute?
steps.stepSummary: רבא gently scolds רפרם. Why take sides in an argument when saying 'המבורך' works for everyone?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: 'Black pot!' Why do you need to get involved in the argument?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא criticizes רפרם's choice. 'Black pot' is an affectionate nickname for a hard-working Torah scholar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל's wording, 'ברכו את ה׳ המבורך', includes all of רבי עקיבא's words and adds 'המבורך'. Saying it satisfies both opinions. Leaving it out needlessly picks one side.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Black pot', a fond nickname for a dedicated scholar

phrases.english: Rava said:
You black pot,
why do you involve yourself in this dispute?

steps.triggerLanguage: פַּתְיָא אוּכָּמָא, בַּהֲדֵי פְּלוּגְתָּא לְמָה לְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא reacts to רפרם's conduct in step 34.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Saying 'המבורך' is acceptable to both opinions, so there is no reason to take a side.

steps.title: Common practice follows רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds a second reason: the accepted practice is to follow רבי ישמעאל and say 'המבורך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also, the common practice is to follow רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives an extra reason against רפרם and closes the story. The custom everywhere is to say 'ברכו את ה׳ המבורך'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason was that 'המבורך' satisfies everyone. This second reason adds that the community's custom has already settled on רבי ישמעאל's wording. So in shul we say 'ברכו את ה׳ המבורך'.

keyTerms.meaning: The common practice of the people

steps.whatToRemember: For ברכו in shul, we say 'ברכו את ה׳ המבורך', following רבי ישמעאל and common practice.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not contradict step 26. There, רבא ruled like רבי עקיבא on a different question: whether the זימון wording changes with crowd size. Here the question is the shul wording, where practice follows רבי ישמעאל. רפרם's mistake was carrying the 'follow רבי עקיבא' ruling over to this second argument.

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד, הָא נְהוּג עָלְמָא כְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל.
phrases.english: Furthermore, the standard practice is in accordance with Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, הָא נְהוּג עָלְמָא כְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second reason to רבא's criticism in step 35 and settles the practice.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In shul we say 'ברכו את ה׳ המבורך', following רבי ישמעאל and accepted practice.

steps.title: When a group that ate together may split up
steps.stepSummary: Three, four, or five who ate together may not split up. Six to nine may split. Ten may not split until there are twenty.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Three people who ate as one group may not split up. The same is true for four and for five. Six, up to ten, may split up. Ten may not split up until there are twenty.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches when people who ate together are allowed to split into smaller groups for bentching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that you may split only if every smaller group can still make the same זימון the big group would have made. Six can become 3 + 3, and both halves still have a זימון of three. Ten use the special wording with God's name (אלקינו), and splitting ten loses that. Only twenty can become 10 + 10 with that wording intact.
steps.whatToRemember: A group may split only if each smaller group keeps the same level of זימון: three can be split off from six, and ten from twenty.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Six up to ten' means six, seven, eight, or nine. Ten itself is NOT included, and ten may not split.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Three who ate as one
are not permitted to split up.
And the same for four, and the same for five.
Six may split up, until ten.
phrases.notes: Six through nine, since each half still has three.

phrases.english: And ten may not split up, until twenty.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה שֶׁאָכְלוּ כְּאַחַת אֵינָן רַשָּׁאִין לֵיחָלֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous discussion about the wording 'ברכו את ה׳ המבורך'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A group that ate together may split only if each smaller group can make the same זימון: 3-5 may not split, 6-9 may split, and 10-19 may not split.

steps.title: Two groups in one house joining for זימון
steps.stepSummary: Two groups eating in one house join for זימון if some of them can see each other. If not, each group makes its own זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two groups that were eating in one house: if some of them can see each other, they join together for זימון. If not, each group makes a זימון for itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second rule: when two separate groups count as one group for זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being in the same house is not enough. What makes two groups one is that some people from each group can see each other. Without that, they are treated as two separate meals.

keyTerms.meaning: Some of them, part of them
For the invitation to bentch together

phrases.english: Two groups that were eating
in one house,

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁמִּקְצָתָן רוֹאִין אֵלּוּ אֶת אֵלּוּ —
phrases.english: when some of them can see each other
they join together for a זימון,
and if not,
these make a זימון for themselves
and those make a זימון for themselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתֵּי חֲבוּרוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹכְלוֹת בְּבַיִת אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second rule in the same משנה about who counts together for זימון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two groups in one house combine for זימון only if some members of each can see each other.

steps.title: Blessing on wine before water is added
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says you do not bless on wine until water is added. חכמים say you do bless.
steps.simpleTranslation: One does not bless over wine until water is put into it. These are the words of רבי אליעזר. חכמים say: one does bless.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a third topic: a מחלוקת about blessing on strong, undiluted wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In those days wine was very strong and was usually mixed with water. רבי אליעזר holds that undiluted wine is not proper drinking wine, so it does not get its proper ברכה. חכמים hold it can still be drunk, so it gets its ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא, the first opinion here

phrases.english: One does not bless over the wine
until he puts water into it,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
And the Sages say: one does bless.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מְבָרְכִין עַל הַיַּיִן עַד שֶׁיִּתֵּן לְתוֹכוֹ מַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate topic in the same משנה about wine instead of זימון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: no ברכה on wine until water is added. חכמים: one does bless on it.

steps.title: Why repeat that three must make a זימון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה is teaching, since we already learned that three who ate together must make a זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is it teaching us? We already learned this once: three who ate as one must make a זימון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and challenges the first line of the משנה. It seems to repeat an earlier משנה, so what is new? This sets up an answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier משנה already said three who ate together are obligated in זימון. If they must make a זימון, it seems obvious they may not split up. So the line 'three may not split' looks like an unneeded repeat.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? (asks what is new)
Are obligated to make a זימון

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is it teaching us?
We already learned it once,
Three who ate as one are obligated to make a זימון!
phrases.notes: Quoting the first משנה of this chapter (45a).

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן תְּנֵינָא חֲדָא זִימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא's first comment on the משנה, aimed at its opening rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's opening line: 'three who ate as one may not split up'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy: an earlier משנה already taught that three who ate together must make a זימון, which seems to include the rule that they may not split up.

steps.title: The obligation starts once three sit down, even before eating
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches the ruling of רבי אבא in the name of שמואל: three who sat down to eat together may not split up, even though they have not eaten yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה teaches us, like what רבי אבא said in the name of שמואל: three people who sat down to eat together, and have not yet eaten, are not allowed to split up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 40. The משנה is not repeating itself. It teaches that the זימון obligation begins as soon as three people sit down to eat together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this, we might think the obligation starts only after the three have actually eaten together. The משנה's wording 'who ate' is read as including people who have only sat down to eat. Sitting down together already makes them one group, and they may not split up to bless alone.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
To split up (and each bless alone)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean they make a זימון before eating. It means they are already locked in as a group, so once they eat they must bless together.

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:
phrases.notes: Standard answer to 'what is the משנה teaching?'

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: like what Rabbi Abba said in the name of Shmuel:
three who sat down to eat together,
and have not yet eaten,
are not allowed to split up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 40 about what the משנה adds.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the משנה adds something new: the obligation starts from the moment of sitting down.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The זימון obligation applies only after the three have actually eaten together.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sitting down together to eat already creates the obligation.

steps.title: Second version: even when each eats from his own loaf
steps.stepSummary: In another version of רבי אבא's report from שמואל, the משנה teaches that three who sat together may not split up, even if each one eats his own bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: רבי אבא said in the name of שמואל that this is what the משנה teaches: three who sat down to eat together, even if each one eats from his own loaf, are not allowed to split up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of what שמואל said about the משנה's new point. Here the new point is that the three do not need to share food to count as one group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought a group is formed only by sharing the same bread. This version says sitting together at one meal is enough, even if each person has separate food. The answer to step 40 is still that the משנה adds something new, but the new point is different.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of the same statement

phrases.english: Another version:
Rabbi Abba said in the name of Shmuel,
this is what the Mishnah teaches:
three who sat down to eat together,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד
phrases.english: even though each and every one
eats from his own loaf,
are not allowed to split up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different version of step 41's answer, with a different new point.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the משנה adds something new: sharing food is not required to form a group.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A group for זימון is formed only by sharing the same bread.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even three people each eating his own loaf, sitting together, form one group.

steps.title: רב הונא's case: three who came from three different groups
steps.stepSummary: Another possibility is that the משנה teaches the ruling of רב הונא: three people who came from three different groups and sat together may not split up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or else, the משנה teaches the ruling of רב הונא, who said: three people who came from three different groups are not allowed to split up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another possible new point in the משנה. It is a case where each of the three left a different group and they then joined together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might think these three cannot form a זימון because they did not start the meal together. רב הונא teaches that they do form a new group and may not split up. This is another way to explain why the משנה is not repeating itself.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי כִּי הָא דְּרַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: Alternatively, like that ruling of Rav Huna,
as Rav Huna said:
three who came from three different groups,
are not allowed to split up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי כִּי הָא דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further alternative answer to the question in step 40.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the משנה adds something new: people from different groups can merge into one group.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: People who did not start the meal together cannot make a זימון together.
steps.terutzMaskana: Three who came from three separate groups and sat together form one group and may not split up.

steps.title: רב חסדא's limit: only if each came from a group of three
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא limits רב הונא's ruling: it applies only if each person came from a group of three, which already had a זימון obligation. Then רבא begins a comment that continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: this applies only when they came from three groups that each had three people. רבא said:
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא narrows רב הונא's rule to one specific case. The last words, 'רבא said', set up a new statement that continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב חסדא, each person carries over the זימון obligation he already had in his first group of three. If a person came from a smaller group with no זימון obligation, רב הונא's rule does not apply to him. רבא is about to add his own comment on this.

keyTerms.meaning: And that is only when… (introduces a limit)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the זימון obligation can carry over with each person from his original group. That is why people from different groups can still be required to bless together.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
and that is only when they came from three groups
of three people each.
Rava said:
phrases.notes: Introduces רבא's statement, which continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רב הונא's ruling from step 43.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא's rule applies only if each of the three came from a group of three that was already obligated in זימון.
